tasks.short: Observe grinding operations and correct problems

steps.what: Observe machine operations and investigate unusual sound, finish, vibration or behaviour
Make permitted adjustments and verify that the operating problem is corrected

tasks.design: Keep observation and permitted corrections with the operator. Existing instructions in {DOCS} remain references; no automatic machine control or labour reduction is proposed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Machine condition must be understood in its physical context.
tasks.enabler_now: Production counters do not replace diagnosis or correction.
tasks.still_hard: Wheel condition, vibration and surface defects may have several causes.
tasks.human_edge: The operator combines sensory evidence with practical process knowledge.
tasks.altitude: No change to the operator's attention or adjustment authority.

reach.learn: Grinding defect diagnosis and escalation limits

evidence.claim: The digest's machine-monitoring capability records quantities and statuses; it does not establish automated grinding diagnosis or corrective control.
Retaining observation and correction effort is an E1 task-boundary judgement, not a measured automation result.

assumptions: Boundary is operator observation and permitted adjustment, excluding maintenance repair and production reporting.
No machine step is introduced, so there is no new structured capture contract. Existing operating instructions remain unchanged upstream.
No implementation or new upkeep is proposed; incremental hours are zero.
research_questions: Which observed faults require a stop or maintenance specialist rather than operator correction?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=100 and zero upkeep. All physical observation and corrections remain unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Study blueprints and determine grinding requirements

steps.what: Study blueprints and machining instructions to determine specifications, tooling and operational sequence

tasks.design: Retain direct study of the released blueprint and instructions in {DOCS}. No generated summary substitutes for interpreting tolerances, symbols and the required operation sequence.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requirements are spread across drawings, notes and instructions.
tasks.enabler_now: Searchable files aid access but do not demonstrate less interpretation time here.
tasks.still_hard: Ambiguous tolerances and conflicting revisions need engineering clarification.
tasks.human_edge: The operator recognises how drawing requirements translate to the actual setup.
tasks.altitude: No change in study effort or authority over engineering requirements.

evidence.claim: Direct interpretation of grinding requirements remains skilled work; no retrieval or transcription saving is assumed without an observed separate step.

assumptions: Boundary is understanding released job requirements, excluding physically selecting or mounting tooling.
Engineering produces the released drawing, work order and instructions upstream; their existing preparation stays unchanged. No machine action requires new structured fields.
No new tool or maintenance is introduced; upkeep is zero.
research_questions: Is searching for the released revision a separately observed bottleneck?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=100, zero upkeep. Skilled interpretation remains unchanged; no document-search baseline is invented.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Select machine tooling using workpiece, machine and production requirements and actual tool condition

tasks.design: Keep tooling selection with the operator, using approved reference information in {DOCS} when needed. No catalogue recommendation removes examination of actual tooling or responsibility for compatibility.
tasks.previous_blocker: Correct tooling depends on material, finish, machine limits and tool condition.
tasks.enabler_now: No new capability in the digest establishes autonomous grinding-tool selection.
tasks.still_hard: A nominally compatible tool may be unsuitable because of wear or the specific job.
tasks.human_edge: The operator understands the actual tooling and production setup.
tasks.altitude: No change to tooling-selection effort or authority.

evidence.claim: Tool suitability is retained as a skilled selection judgement; the digest's gear-calculation capability does not establish grinding-tool selection savings.

assumptions: Boundary starts with understood machining requirements and ends with selected tooling, excluding earlier blueprint study and later setup.
Engineering supplies existing machining requirements, and the operator examines existing tools within s1. No machine step needs newly structured inputs.
No new system or upkeep is introduced, so incremental hours are zero.
unknowns: Tool types and approved compatibility rules
research_questions: Which selection decisions depend on actual tool condition rather than catalogue fields?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=100 and zero upkeep. The actual selection judgement is unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Repair machine parts or notify engineering

steps.what: Assess the fault and repair or replace machine parts within authorised maintenance limits
Notify engineering of unresolved faults and explain the repair actions already taken

tasks.design: Keep permitted repairs and engineering escalation with the operator. Reference instructions may remain in {DOCS}; no repair-time saving follows from digitising a notification alone.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repair needs physical access, diagnosis and appropriate authority.
tasks.enabler_now: Production-data collection does not perform the repair.
tasks.still_hard: Fault causes and safe return to service require competent examination.
tasks.human_edge: The operator recognises limits and describes what actually happened.
tasks.altitude: No change to repair effort or engineering responsibilities.

reach.learn: Fault reporting and authorised repair boundaries

evidence.claim: Physical part replacement and contextual engineering notification remain human work; no repetitive clerical stage is assumed.

assumptions: Boundary is operator-authorised repair and escalation, excluding engineering repairs and formal return-to-service decisions; their existing work is unchanged.
The operator produces repair observations during retained s1 and explains them in retained s2. No structured discrepancy code or automated notification is presumed.
No implementation or additional upkeep is introduced, so incremental hours are zero.
research_questions: Which faults must be escalated before attempting any operator repair?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=100 and zero upkeep. Repair and escalation effort remain unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: No new control authority or reduction in machine attention follows from this task set.
reach: Work with machinists on defect recognition
Support supervisors with clear fault escalation
role.ambitious_version: A skilled operator who focuses on stable machining and clear escalation; no speculative labour saving is assigned.
